scenes.line1: How do streams handle late data?
scenes.say: Ever wondered how streaming systems handle late or out-of-order events and still give accurate results?

scenes.label: Windows
scenes.sub: Group events by time or count for processing
scenes.say: First up, windows. These group events into chunks, like every five minutes or every hundred records, so you can run analytics on each batch.

scenes.label: Watermarks
scenes.sub: Track event time progress, handle lateness
scenes.say: Next, watermarks. They track how far event time has moved, letting the system know when to close a window, even if some events arrive late.
State is crucial. It stores running results, lets you join related events, and helps update the output when late data arrives.

scenes.question: What if watermarks are too strict?
scenes.right: Late events might be dropped, so you could lose data.
scenes.say: Here's a common trap: if your watermark is too strict, late events might get dropped, and you could lose important data.
